regulation.title: Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 betreffende maatregelen voor een hoog gezamenlijk niveau van cyberbeveiliging in de Unie, tot wijziging van Verordening (EU) nr. 910/2014 en Richtlijn (EU) 2018/1972 en tot intrekking van Richtlijn (EU) 2016/1148 (NIS2-richtlijn)
regulation.date_end_of_validity_note: Standard EU sentinel for 'no defined expiration date' -- same pattern already confirmed for DORA.
regulation.type: Richtlijn (EU) -- NOT a Regulation, unlike the AI Act, GDPR and DORA
regulation.addressed_to: EUMS (European Union Member States) -- direct metadata confirmation of NIS2's Directive nature; Regulations in this project's corpus (AI Act, GDPR, DORA) do not carry this 'addresses' relationship since they apply directly rather than requiring implementation by an addressee.
regulation.treaty_legal_basis: TFEU Article 114 (internal market harmonization) -- found via 'based_on', not previously captured.

internal_workflow_tag.note: An internal Publications Office processing tag (resource_legal_comment_internal); meaning not documented anywhere in this metadata file, preserved as found rather than guessed at.

regulation.responsible_commission_department: CNECT (DG Communications Networks, Content and Technology) -- same department responsible for the AI Act.
regulation.structural_note: NIS2 is a DIRECTIVE, requiring national transposition -- this is structurally different from the three prior EU laws processed for this project (all Regulations, directly applicable). This is precisely why the Cbw (Cyberbeveiligingswet) exists as a separate Dutch dataset in this project: it is NIS2's Dutch transposition. This file's data reflects that difference: it tracks 303 national implementing measures across the EU (see implementing_measures below) and two transposition-deadline dates, categories that do not exist for the three Regulations.
regulation.note: Companion/reference dataset, not a replacement for either uploaded source file. Both legal_text_nl.html and metadata.xml remain untouched at /mnt/user-data/uploads/.

SOURCE_TEXT_CURRENCY_FINDING.finding: Same pattern as DORA: no full amending instrument found for NIS2's own text, but 4 of its 9 corrigenda postdate the HTML's generation date.
SOURCE_TEXT_CURRENCY_FINDING.recommendation: Re-fetch NIS2's text from EUR-Lex and diff against the uploaded HTML before treating any provision as certainly current.

national_implementing_measures.IMPORTANT_LIMITATION: All 303 target records are bare stub identifiers (opaque 'nim/NNNNNN' numbers) carrying ONLY generic RDF type declarations -- no country, no national law title, no BWB-id or equivalent, no date, in either the direct triples or their reified copies (confirmed: the 303 reified 'implemented_by' annotation records carry zero additional detail beyond the direct triples). This metadata file can confirm THAT 303 national measures are tracked for NIS2, but CANNOT identify WHICH measure corresponds to which country or law. The Dutch Cbw's BWB-id (BWBR0052872) was explicitly searched for among these 303 identifiers and was not found in any resolvable form -- this is a genuine data limitation of this file, not a failed search; confirming Cbw's specific presence among the 303 would require a different EUR-Lex service (the National Transposition Measures database), not this metadata dump.

transposition_deadline.note: Both dates are recorded in the source metadata itself, under BOTH 'date_transposition' and 'directive_date_transposition' predicates, with no indication of which is canonical -- this is not an extraction ambiguity on my part, both values are genuinely present side-by-side in the data. Publicly, 17 October 2024 is the widely-cited NIS2 transposition deadline; the 18 October value may reflect a different calculation basis (e.g. the literal calendar date of the 21-month statutory period vs. a rounded/administrative date). Reported as found rather than resolved to a single value.

amendments_to_own_text.note: Same category of finding as GDPR and DORA -- no amendment to NIS2's own substantive text found.

repeals.name: The original NIS1 Directive (2016/1148) -- NIS2's direct predecessor
repeals.note: Effective on (one of) the transposition dates -- confirms the repeal of NIS1 was timed to coincide with NIS2's transposition deadline, not its earlier entry-into-force date.

items.note: A proposed DIRECTIVE -- distinct from the Digital Omnibus proposal below, likely a NIS2-specific amendment.

CONFIRMED (not just inferred, as it was for GDPR): this is the IDENTICAL document ID found as GDPR's own pending proposal during that dataset's build. This is hard proof, not speculation, that a single Commission proposal -- almost certainly the Digital Omnibus simplification package -- touches both GDPR and NIS2 simultaneously. This upgrades the GDPR companion file's earlier note (which only flagged 'numerically close to the AI Act's own proposal' as circumstantial) to a confirmed cross-instrument fact.

adopts.name: The original European Commission proposal for NIS2

basis_for.note: 10 of these 21 entries are NIS2's own consolidated-version history (base + 9 sub-versions, matching the 9 corrigenda exactly). Reified duplicates for 3 of the remaining 11 add no new detail (confirmed: no location or date on any of the 7 reified basis_for records).

verified_directly_against_nis2_text.AR = Artikel: confirmed (the only code actually used in NIS2's own extracted location data)
verified_directly_against_nis2_text.PA = lid: confirmed present in running text, 252 occurrences, though not needed for NIS2's own 3 amendment locations

decode_terminology_verification.notable_absence: Unlike the AI Act, GDPR, and DORA, NIS2 has ZERO occurrences of 'Afdeling' -- its chapters are not subdivided that way. It DOES have Annexes (3 'BIJLAGE' occurrences), unlike GDPR and DORA which have none -- almost certainly NIS2's own Annexes I and II (sector lists for essential/important entities), which are very likely the EU-level source underlying the Cbw's own Bijlage 1 and 2 already in this project's corpus. Not independently cross-checked article-by-article against Cbw's annexes in this pass.

subject_matter_classification.note: Raw EU classification metadata (EuroVoc concepts, subject-matter domain codes, directory codes) describing what NIS2 is 'about'. Preserved per the no-information-loss requirement, but NOT confidently decoded into plain-language meanings except where genuinely certain -- guessing at EuroVoc numeric-concept meanings without a lookup table risks introducing exactly the kind of fabricated-but-plausible error this process is meant to avoid.

subject_matter_domain_codes.TECN: Technology (high confidence -- standard EUR-Lex subject-matter domain abbreviation)
subject_matter_domain_codes.ELSJ: Likely 'area of freedom, security and justice' domain -- moderately confident, not independently verified against an authority table
subject_matter_domain_codes.PDON: Meaning not confidently known -- preserved as-is rather than guessed
